note: WebSearch returned result titles and links only (no snippets), so web results were judged by title, and nothing was opened. "Lampyris flicker fusion" returned the pages of Inger et al. 2014 (DOAJ, PMC4038456, the PLoS ONE page and the Bangor, Monash and Plymouth research portals) and the Wikipedia article on the flicker fusion threshold. "glow-worm flicker fusion" returned an untitled Springer record (BF02160841), the systematic review of Lafitte et al. 2022 (PMC9803175), Inger et al. 2014 again, two MeSH descriptor pages and a profile page, a rat superior colliculus preprint, a patent and an Oxford slide record. No title names a flicker or photoreceptor-speed measurement for a glow-worm or for any other firefly. Main holds the flicker species of Inger et al. 2014 and Lafitte et al. 2022, and screen_candidates.py finds no Lampyris row on main for either flicker trait; main's one firefly flicker value is that of Photinus pyralis (oa-1, 40 Hz), another genus. Booth, Stewart and Osorio 2004 (the top hit of "Lampyris vision") was opened by main's sweep-53, which logged its acceptance angle for Lampyris noctiluca males and found no other eye value. The 2015 review of the firefly visual system (10.1007/s13127-015-0212-z, a family-review hit with no stored abstract) is on main's insect wanted list for eye types, receptor classes and night sensitivity; its title promises opsin genes and colour vision, and nothing in it or in main's line points to a flicker or photoreceptor-speed value, so it holds back no flicker cell (my judgement). acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg have no record: they wait on this unit's wanted list for that review and for a University of Connecticut dissertation on mapping firefly compound eyes, whose species are not shown. Haarlem et al. 2026 (flicker fusion over 237 species) is in the canon file and unread, so this record stays half-searched until it is logged (desk-screen.md point 8); the books by Warrant and Nilsson (2006) and Cronin et al. (2014) are not in hand either.
